s003:
The camera is the scanner, so there’s no hardware to buy. Point it at anything with
            a printed barcode and the name, photo and description fill themselves in. Three taps per
            thing, whether that’s a kitchen cupboard or a stockroom.
s004: Free to install. Sign in with Google. No form, no password.
s005: How it works, from empty to up to date.
s007: Name it whatever you like and the app builds a Google Spreadsheet for it in your own Drive.
s009: A pantry needs expiry dates, a workshop serial numbers. Add the fields your things have, in eight types including dropdowns with your own options, and the sheet grows columns to match.
s011: The camera reads the barcode and the name, photo and description arrive filled in. Choose which location it lives in, save, and the product exists.
s013: Scan the barcode a second time and it opens that product, or type any part of the name.
s015: The quantity it already has comes straight up. Thumb it up or down, save, move on.
s080: Put an expiry, warranty or service date on a product and the app pushes or emails you before it passes. Set a floor on a quantity and it tells you when you go below it. This is the one step you do nothing for.
s018: The same app, on both sides of the door.
s020: Know what is in the cupboard while you are standing in the shop.
s109: Food and medicine stop running out or going out of date unnoticed.
s022: A collection becomes searchable: books, board games, wine, tools.
s023: The garage, the loft and the shed each get their own list.
s025: Stocktake is a walk down the shelf with the phone you already carry.
s026: Tell a customer what you have without going to look.
s027: Supplier, serial number, warranty end: add the columns your trade needs.
s028: Up to five people work from the same list, and history shows who changed what.

s032: Tap the green circle, point the camera at a barcode, and the app searches global product databases. The name, description and photo come back filled in, in your language. Tap Save & scan next and the camera is already back up.
s033:
There is no hardware to buy. No scanner gun, nothing to pair, nothing to charge. It
              reads twelve barcode formats, zooms itself in on small print, and beeps so you can keep
              your eyes on the shelf.
s034: No barcode? Add it by hand in a few seconds.
s035: Own-brand and unlabelled stock scans fine and comes back blank, and you type the name.

s038:
Import a CSV and your column headers are matched to the right fields automatically, so

s040: Three ways back to one thing.
s041: Scan it again. The second scan is a stocktake: the app shows the number you had and waits. Thumb it up or down, save, and the camera comes back. Walk the shelf and the count is done before you sit down.
s042: Search reads more than the name. Type half a barcode, a word from the description or a supplier you typed into a field of your own, and it finds the item.
s043: Locations view turns each place into a folder. Tap Pantry, see what is in Pantry. Anything unfiled sits in Without location rather than disappearing.
s133: Nothing decrements on its own. There is no till feed, so if you sell things all day this count will drift. A low-stock alert works from the number you last saved, not from what has left the shelf since.
s047: Products, locations, total stock and the last thing that changed, on one screen.
s049: Prices, dates, serial numbers. Eight types, and each becomes a real column in the sheet.
s144: A date on a product, and it tells you days before it passes, by push or email. A floor on a quantity, and it tells you when stock drops below it.
s053: Invite up to four other people. Everyone works from the same list.
s055: What changed, who did it and when. Every quantity moved, every product added or deleted.
s056: It’s a Google Sheet. In your Drive.
s057:
The first time you sign in, 1inventory creates a real spreadsheet in your own Google Drive.
          Every product you add is a row in it. Open it on a laptop, sort it, chart it, or share it

s157: Why not just use a Google Sheet directly?
s158:
You are: that’s the design. What the app adds is a camera, a global product
            database, a folder view with a count per shelf, a quantity stepper you can hit
            with a thumb, and columns that arrive already named and formatted. Try typing a
            13-digit barcode into a cell on a phone. That is the part we removed.
s159: Do I need a Google account? Can I sign up with an email address?
s160: Yes, and it is the only sign-in the app uses. The upside is that signing up takes one tap: there is no form to fill in and no password to invent, and your first spreadsheet exists before you reach the home screen.
s161: Why does an inventory app need access to my Google Drive?
s162: It asks for drive.file, the narrowest Drive permission Google offers. An app holding it can touch only the files it created itself, so 1inventory can open the spreadsheet and photo folder it made for you and nothing besides. Google enforces that boundary. Gmail, Calendar and the rest of your account stay out of reach.
s163: Will the scanner recognise my things?
s164: Shop-bought goods with retail barcodes come back with a name, description and photo: tins, jars, medicine, ISBN books, board games, Lego, DVDs, batteries. Own-brand and warehouse labels scan fine too, the lookup simply has nothing to fill in, so you type the name. Twelve barcode formats are supported, and scanning itself is unlimited; only the database lookups are capped, at 5 a day on Free and 200 on Premium.
s165: Is there a web app? Does it work on an iPad?
s166: Your data is fully usable on a laptop: the spreadsheet opens in Google Sheets like any other file, where you can sort, filter, chart and print it. The app itself is a portrait phone app for iOS 15.6 and later and Android 7.0 and later, so there is no tablet layout or browser client today.
s167: What about the list you already keep?
s168: I already have a list. Do I have to retype it?
s169: No. Import a CSV and your column headers are matched to fields by meaning, so a sheet headed Item / Qty / Where lands in the right columns with no setup. Limits: CSV only, 5 MB, 60 columns, a name column required. The mapping runs in one pass and is shown to you afterwards. Duplicates are skipped.
s170: How many products can I have?
s171:
As many as you like, on the free plan and on Premium alike — the number of
            products has never been what you pay for. What Premium adds is more inventories,
            more people on them, more of your own fields and the change history.
s172: Limits, and what we’re working on
s174: Not yet, and it’s on the way. Every action is a network call today, so you need a connection to add or change something. Offline is coming in a future release, and it matters most in cellars, garages, lock-ups and vans, which is exactly where an inventory tends to live.
s175: Will it tell me when I’m running low?
s176: Not right now. Today’s alerts watch dates rather than quantities: put an expiry, a warranty end or a service date on a product and you get a push notification or an email a set number of days before that date, or after it. Quantity-based alerts are an extension we’re working on.
s177: What if I need more than five people?
s178: Five people is what the app is built around: a household, a workshop, or a small crew. Places are not capped on Premium, but they sit side by side rather than nesting, and everyone you invite gets the same level of access. If you need warehouse zones inside zones, per-location permissions or a read-only role, a larger system will serve you better.
s180: Is it safe to let my partner or a colleague in?
s181: Yes. They sign in with their own Google account, and where the inventory has a History tab every change lands there with their name on it. Worth knowing: there are two roles rather than a read-only option, so anyone you invite can edit and delete. Inviting needs Premium, the cap is five people including you, and the spreadsheet stays in your Drive alone.
s182: Will their changes appear on my phone straight away?
s183: Changes reach your Google Sheet as soon as they are saved. On another phone they appear when the list is pulled down to refresh, rather than updating live while you are looking at it. If two people count the same shelf at the same moment, the last one saved wins.

s187: What happens if I stop paying?
s188:
Nothing is deleted. Extra inventories, locations, custom fields and the people

s191: Most of what follows has the same answer: the file is already in your Drive.
s194:
There is no export button, because there is nothing to export. Your inventory is
            already a Google Sheet in your own Drive, and Google will save it out as CSV,
            Excel or PDF whenever you like. One caveat: the file lives in the inventory
            owner’s Drive, so this is something owners can do and invited people
            cannot.
s195: What if I delete something by accident?
s196: Your inventory is a Google Sheet, so it inherits Google Drive’s version history. The app’s Backups screen lists the revisions and walks you through restoring one; the restore itself happens in Google Sheets rather than in the app. One thing to note: deleting a custom field removes that whole column from your spreadsheet, values included.
s198:
The spreadsheet, its history tab and the photo folder are in your Google Drive
            and stay there, readable by anything that opens a spreadsheet. What you would
            lose is the scanner, the barcode lookup and the folder view. We can promise
            continuity of data, not continuity of service.

s226: Something wrong? Here’s how to reach a person.
s227: Two routes, and the one inside the app is quicker, because it arrives already carrying the details we would otherwise have to write back and ask you for.
s228: In the app: Settings → Support. Pick one of four categories: Feature Request, Bug Report, Billing Question, General Question. Say what happened. Send.
s229: A confirmation appears on screen and an acknowledgement email follows. The request itself goes to a channel that people at Sparkybit read.
s231: An email carries none of the diagnostics the in-app form attaches, so it is worth including what is on the list further down this page.
s232: What an in-app report carries with it
s233: The form asks you for one thing: a description. It sends a good deal more than that, automatically, so that a bug report arrives in a state we can reproduce.

s247: Worth thirty seconds before you write to us.
s248: “Required columns are missing in Google Sheet table Products.” Somebody renamed, moved or deleted a column in the spreadsheet. Open the sheet and put the header back exactly as the message spells it out.
s249: A whole tab has gone. Delete nothing else, then pull down to refresh. The app rebuilds a missing tab with the right headers. It cannot bring back what was in it; for that, use File → Version history in Google Sheets.
s250: Nothing loads at all. Every action needs a connection. There is no offline mode.
s251: Someone else’s change is not showing. Pull down to refresh. Your phone is showing you what it last read, and refreshing is what makes it read again.
s252: A barcode came back empty. Not every product is in the public databases, and a free account gets five lookups a day against two hundred on Premium. Add the item by hand and it behaves exactly like a scanned one from then on.
s253: An import skipped rows. Importing only ever inserts. A row matching something already in your inventory is skipped and the product you have is left untouched.
s254: File → Version history is a Google Sheets feature. It lives in the spreadsheet’s own File menu, it goes back further than most people expect, and it is the only route to data that was in a tab before the tab disappeared.

s276:
Sparkybit GmbH (“we,” “us,” or “our”) is committed to protecting
        your personal data. This Privacy Policy outlines our practices for collecting, storing, using, and
        protecting your information when you use our 1inventory mobile application, our server-side services,
        and their interactions with your Google Drive (collectively, the “Services”).
s277: As the “controller” in the sense of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), we are responsible for protecting your personal data. Our data protection team will be happy to assist you with any questions you may have about data processing, your rights, or this privacy policy statement. It can be reached at: gdpr@1inventory.io.
s279: We collect information to provide and improve our Services. The types of information we collect are:
s281: Account Information: When you register for our Services using your Google Account, we collect your first name, last name, email address, and the URL of your profile picture. Authentication is handled entirely by Google; we do not process your Google password.
s283: User Data: We store your name, email, profile picture URL, and settings for any custom fields you create within the app.
s284: Google API Tokens: To connect to your Google account, we store access and refresh tokens. These tokens are kept in an encrypted format.
s285: Inventory Data: The actual data for your inventories is stored directly within Google Sheets on your personal Google Drive. This data passes through our server, which acts as a proxy, but it is not stored or cached on our servers.
s287: Usage Analytics: We use Firebase Analytics to collect statistics on how users interact with our mobile application. This helps us understand usage patterns and improve the service.
s289: We use the information we collect for the following purposes:
s290: To Provide and Maintain the Service: We use your Google API tokens to access the specific Google Sheets created by our application, allowing you to manage your inventory.
s291: To Personalize Your Experience: We use your account information to identify you within the application.
s292: For Service Improvement: We analyze usage data through Firebase Analytics to understand what features are used most and to guide future development.
s293: To Communicate with You: We may use your email address to send you important information about the Services.
s295: We do not sell your personal information. We may share your information only in the following circumstances:
s296: With Service Providers: Our application is hosted on Microsoft Azure. We also use Google’s Firebase service for analytics. These providers have access to data only as necessary to perform their functions.
s297: For Legal Reasons: We may disclose your information if required by law or in response to a valid legal process.
s298: Business Transfers: In the event of a merger, acquisition, or sale of assets, your information may be transferred to the new entity.
s300: We implement strong security measures to protect your data.
s301: The access and refresh tokens we store are encrypted in our database using robust encryption standards like AES 256.
s302: Access to user data requires compromising multiple security layers, including the database, the decryption keys, and our application’s unique client-id and client-secret.
s303: The permissions granted to our application are non-sensitive and limited to accessing your profile and email, and managing only the files that our application creates in your Google Drive. We utilize the Google People API, Drive API, and Sheets API for these purposes.
s305:
We do not have a set data retention period and will store your information as long as your account is
        active. You can delete your account at any time. Upon receiving a deletion request, we will remove all
        personal data associated with your account from our servers.
s306:
Please note that Google may automatically revoke an API refresh token if it has not been used for six
        months, which would require you to re-authenticate.
s307: 6. Your Rights Under GDPR (UK & EEA Residents)
s308:
We comply with the GDPR. If you are a resident of the European Economic Area (EEA) or the UK, you have
        the following rights regarding your personal data:
s309: Right to Access: You have the right to request a copy of the information we hold about you.
s310: Right to Rectification: You have the right to correct any inaccurate or incomplete data.
s311: Right to Erasure (“Right to be Forgotten”): You can request the deletion of your personal data. You can perform this action yourself at any time using the “Delete my account” function in your profile, which will remove all of your data from our systems.
s312: Right to Restrict Processing: You have the right to request that we limit the processing of your data under certain conditions.
s313: Right to Data Portability: You have the right to receive your data in a structured, machine-readable format.
s314: Right to Object: You have the right to object to our processing of your data.
s317:
Our servers are located in Europe and the US. Therefore, your data may be transferred to and stored in
        countries outside of your country of residence, including outside the EEA. We ensure that such transfers
        comply with applicable laws and that your data is protected to the standard required within the EEA.
s319:
Our services are not intended for or directed at children, and we do not knowingly collect any personal

s421:
The sections above describe the 1inventory mobile application. This section covers the website
        itself, which is operated separately and collects considerably less.
s423: We use Google Analytics 4 to understand how the site is used — which pages are read, which links are followed, and how far down a page visitors get. It runs in a cookieless mode: Google’s consent settings are set to deny all storage before the analytics code loads, so no analytics cookies are written and nothing is stored on your device. That is why this site does not ask you to accept cookies.
s424:
Because nothing identifying is stored on your device, we cannot recognise you from one visit to
          the next. Visitor and session figures are therefore estimates rather than counts of people.
s425: What is sent: the page address and its language, your device and browser type, an approximate location derived from your IP address, and the interactions described above — following a link to the App Store or Google Play, switching language, jumping to a section, and how far you scrolled. The IP address is used to derive the approximate location and is not stored by Google Analytics.
s426: What is not sent: your name, your email address, or any inventory data. The website has no accounts, no forms and no sign-in.
s428:
If you pick a language from the switcher, that choice is saved in your browser’s local
          storage so later pages open in the language you chose, and a separate temporary entry stops the
          site guessing your language twice in one visit. Neither is used for tracking, neither leaves
          your browser, and clearing your browsing data removes both.
s429: Legal basis and processor. Because nothing is stored on or read from your device for analytics purposes, this processing does not require your consent under §25 TTDSG. It rests instead on our legitimate interest in understanding and improving the site, under Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR. Google acts as our processor, and analytics data is retained for 14 months.
s430: Legal pages shown inside the app. When the 1inventory app displays this policy, the terms or the FAQ within the application itself, analytics are not loaded at all.
s431:
You may object to this processing at any time using the contact details below, and most browsers
        offer settings or extensions that block analytics outright.
